# dynaSpec: dynamic spectrogram visualizations

![sketchy sticker](reference/figures/dynaSpec_sticker.png)

**dynaSpec** creates dynamic spectrograms: spectrograms that move along
with the sound, ready for presentations, teaching or sharing online,
*without taking screen recordings* of another program. They are shown as
interactive web pages (with the sound embedded, click-to-play and
buttons to slow the sound down), which work in R Markdown and Quarto
documents, and can also be saved as videos (mp4). It builds on
[seewave](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=seewave) and
[tuneR](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=tuneR).

Dynamic spectrograms are built in layers, as ‘ggplot2’ graphs:
[`dynaspec()`](https://marce10.github.io/dynaSpec/reference/dynaspec.md)
takes the sound, and layers are added with `+` (only the panels added
are shown):

| Layer | What it does |
|----|----|
| [`ds_spectrogram()`](https://marce10.github.io/dynaSpec/reference/ds_spectrogram.md) | Adds a spectrogram (window length, palette, amplitude range, …) |
| [`ds_oscillogram()`](https://marce10.github.io/dynaSpec/reference/ds_oscillogram.md), [`ds_envelope()`](https://marce10.github.io/dynaSpec/reference/ds_envelope.md) | Add an oscillogram or an amplitude envelope (above or below the spectrogram) |
| [`ds_spectrum()`](https://marce10.github.io/dynaSpec/reference/ds_spectrum.md) | Adds a power spectrum next to the spectrogram |
| [`ds_overview()`](https://marce10.github.io/dynaSpec/reference/ds_overview.md) | Adds a lower panel with the whole sound to scrolling spectrograms |
| [`ds_annotations()`](https://marce10.github.io/dynaSpec/reference/ds_annotations.md) | Highlights parts of the sound with translucent boxes, borders and labels (e.g. from a selection table) |
| [`ds_captions()`](https://marce10.github.io/dynaSpec/reference/ds_captions.md) | Text at a fixed position shown during a time range, like subtitles |
| [`ds_theme()`](https://marce10.github.io/dynaSpec/reference/ds_theme.md), [`ds_theme_dark()`](https://marce10.github.io/dynaSpec/reference/ds_theme.md), … | Axis titles, fonts, colors of the figure and plot, and preset themes |
| [`ds_player()`](https://marce10.github.io/dynaSpec/reference/ds_player.md) | Playback controls of web pages (speed slider, loop, volume, download, …) |
| [`ds_static()`](https://marce10.github.io/dynaSpec/reference/styles.md), [`ds_scrolling()`](https://marce10.github.io/dynaSpec/reference/styles.md) or [`ds_paged()`](https://marce10.github.io/dynaSpec/reference/styles.md) | Style of the dynamic spectrogram (see below) |

The package offers three styles of dynamic spectrogram:

| Style | What it looks like |
|----|----|
| Static ([`ds_static()`](https://marce10.github.io/dynaSpec/reference/styles.md), default) | A play line moves over the whole spectrogram (and oscillogram), which can be split in several rows |
| Scrolling ([`ds_scrolling()`](https://marce10.github.io/dynaSpec/reference/styles.md)) | The spectrogram scrolls from right to left past a fixed “play” line, as in the Macaulay Library |
| Paged ([`ds_paged()`](https://marce10.github.io/dynaSpec/reference/styles.md)) | A spectrogram (or several “pages”) revealed by a sliding highlight box, as in Adobe Audition’s spectral view |

**Contents:** [Installation](#installation) · [Quick
start](#quick-start) · [Background](#background) · [Citation](#citation)

> 📖 **Examples of the three styles are in the vignette [Creating
> dynamic
> spectrograms](https://marce10.github.io/dynaSpec/articles/dynaSpec.html)**
> (or run
> [`vignette("dynaSpec")`](https://marce10.github.io/dynaSpec/articles/dynaSpec.md)
> in R). Customization options are shown in the article [Customizing
> dynamic
> spectrograms](https://marce10.github.io/dynaSpec/articles/customizing.html).

## Installation

Install the development version from GitHub (requires
[remotes](https://cran.r-project.org/package=remotes)):

``` r

remotes::install_github("maRce10/dynaSpec")
```

### ffmpeg

Web pages do not need any external software. To create videos dynaSpec
uses [ffmpeg](https://ffmpeg.org/download.html), which must be installed
and available in the system path:

| Operating system | Command (in a terminal) |
|----|----|
| Windows | `winget install --id Gyan.FFmpeg -e` (or download a build from [gyan.dev](https://www.gyan.dev/ffmpeg/builds/) and add its `bin` folder to the PATH) |
| macOS | `brew install ffmpeg` |
| Debian/Ubuntu | `sudo apt install ffmpeg` |

You can check that R finds it with:

``` r

Sys.which("ffmpeg")
```

If ffmpeg is installed somewhere else, point R to the executable with
`Sys.setenv(ffmpeg = "path/to/ffmpeg")`.

## Quick start

``` r

library(dynaSpec)

# example recording included in the package
data("scythebill")

# static spectrogram with oscillogram
# (shown in the RStudio viewer or the web browser)
x <- dynaspec(scythebill, flim = c(1.5, 5.5)) +
  ds_spectrogram(wl = 200, collevels = seq(-50, 0, 1)) +
  ds_oscillogram()

x

# paged style
x + ds_paged(t.display = 1)

# scrolling style (a longer recording)
data("antshrike")
y <- dynaspec(antshrike, flim = c(0.5, 5.5)) +
  ds_spectrogram(wl = 256, collevels = seq(-50, 0, 1))
y + ds_scrolling(t.display = 2)

# save as a web page or as a video
save_dynaspec(x, "scythebill.html")
save_dynaspec(y + ds_scrolling(t.display = 2), "antshrike.mp4")
```

Sounds can be ‘Wave’ objects or ‘.wav’ and ‘.mp3’ files. Invalid
arguments are reported all together before any processing starts, so
mistakes are caught early. See the
[vignette](https://marce10.github.io/dynaSpec/articles/dynaSpec.html)
for many more options and examples.

## Background

This package is a collaboration between [Marcelo
Araya-Salas](https://marce10.github.io/) and [Matt
Wilkins](https://www.mattwilkinsbio.com/), and the successor of
[dynaSpec](https://github.com/maRce10/dynaSpec). The goal is to create
static and dynamic visualizations of sounds, ready for publication or
presentation. Marcelo’s approach (scrolling spectrograms) shows a
spectrogram sliding past a fixed point as sounds are played, similar to
that used in Cornell’s Macaulay Library. Matt’s approach creates “paged”
spectrograms that are revealed by a sliding highlight box as sounds are
played, akin to Adobe Audition’s spectral view. dynaSpec brings both
approaches, and static spectrograms with a moving play line, together
under a single layered syntax, and adds interactive web pages.

A taste of what you can do (a video made with dynaSpec):
